title: Finite locally free infinitesimal neighborhoods of a smooth affine section
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $p:Y\to S$ a smooth affine morphism of finite presentation [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $e:S\to Y$ be a section. Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and let $\epsilon:B\to A$ be the induced $A$-algebra retraction, so $\epsilon\circ(A\to B)=1_A$. Put $J=\ker\epsilon$ and, for $n\geq0$, put $Y_n=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J^{n+1})$, with its quotient-induced closed immersion in $Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $Y_n\to S$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For every commutative $A$-algebra $A'$ let $B'=B\otimes_A A'$ and let $\epsilon':B'\to A'$ be the induced retraction. There is a canonical isomorphism of $A'$-algebras $(B/J^{n+1})\otimes_A A'\simeq B'/(\ker\epsilon')^{n+1}$, compatible with the quotient maps from $B'$. Thus $Y_n\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A'$ is the $n$th infinitesimal neighborhood of the base-changed section [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Conrad, proof of Proposition 2.1.6, printed pp.62--63, finite flat infinitesimal neighborhoods of a section; the statement isolates this part of the proof for an affine smooth scheme. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this exact assertion.

proof.text: Put $k=n+1\geq1$ and write $i:A\to B$ for the structure map. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to the whole affine source and target shows that $B$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] the given smoothness includes formal smoothness. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-formally-smooth-iff-ring-lifting], $A\to B$ has the square-zero algebra lifting property. Together with finite presentation, [lem-weil-pbc-fp-square-zero-lifting-smooth-ring-map] makes it a smooth ring map. These statements apply to arbitrary commutative base rings.

source.place: Tag 02H4, lemma-affine-formally-smooth; algebra.tex Tag 00TN, proposition-smooth-formally-smooth; morphisms.tex Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize

proof.text: Choose finitely many algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ of $B/A$ and replace them by $x_i=b_i-i(\epsilon(b_i))$. They still generate $B$ as an $A$-algebra. If $b=F(x_1,\ldots,x_t)$, then $\epsilon(b)=F(0)$, so $b-i\epsilon(b)=F(x)-F(0)\in(x_1,\ldots,x_t)$. Thus $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_t)$. The ideal $J^k$ is generated by the finitely many products $x^\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=k$. Modulo it every polynomial in the $x_i$ is an $A$-linear combination of the finitely many monomials $x^\alpha$ with $|\alpha|<k$, since a monomial of degree at least $k$ has a degree-$k$ factor. Hence $Q=B/J^k$ is a finite $A$-module.

source.place: Definition Tag 00F3, definition-finite-type; elementary polynomial expansion and ideal multiplication

proof.text: The finitely generated ideal $J^k$ and the finite presentation of $B/A$ satisfy [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal], so $Q$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra. Its finite generation as an $A$-module was proved in Step 2. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-presentation-module-presentation] shows that $Q$ is a finitely presented $A$-module. This is the finiteness of relations needed later; finite generation alone would not suffice over an arbitrary ring.

source.place: Tag 00F4, lemma-compose-finite-type, quotient presentation; Tag 0564, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-extension

proof.text: Fix any $A$-algebra $A'$, write $B'=B\otimes_A A'$, and define $\epsilon'(b\otimes a')=\epsilon(b)a'$. Let $L\subset B'$ be the ideal generated by $j\otimes1$ for $j\in J$. It is killed by $\epsilon'$. Conversely, for $z=\sum_i b_i\otimes a_i'$ with $\epsilon'(z)=0$, the identity $z=\sum_i(b_i-i\epsilon(b_i))\otimes a_i'+1\otimes\sum_i\epsilon(b_i)a_i'$ puts $z$ in $L$. Hence $\ker\epsilon'=L=JB'$. Expanding products of generators gives $L^k=J^kB'$: each product of $k$ generators is the image of a product in $J$, and the image of every generator of $J^k$ is such a product. No injectivity after tensoring an arbitrary exact sequence is being assumed.

source.place: Elementary split-augmentation calculation, with arbitrary scalar extension

proof.text: There are mutually inverse $A'$-algebra maps $Q\otimes_A A'\rightleftarrows B'/L^k$. The forward map sends $\overline b\otimes a'$ to the class of $b\otimes a'$. It is well-defined because the image of $J^k$ is killed. The reverse map is induced by $b\otimes a'\mapsto\overline b\otimes a'$, which kills $L^k=J^kB'$. Both composites fix pure tensors and hence every element. The forward map sends the image of every $b\otimes a'\in B'$ to its quotient class, giving the required compatibility with the quotient maps. This proves the algebra base-change assertion already, and also applies to $A'=A_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$.

source.place: Elementary tensor-product and quotient universal properties; explicit maps

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$. Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $C=B\otimes_A R$ and $I=\ker(C\to R)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], $C$ is smooth over the local ring $R$. The augmentation is still an $R$-algebra retraction. Thus [lem-sbc-smooth-augmentation-first-order-coordinates] supplies $r\geq0$ and $f:R[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to C$ carrying $H=(T_1,\ldots,T_r)$ into $I$ and inducing a bijection modulo their squares. The square-zero lifting of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] also gives the nilpotent lifting required by the next node: if $K^N=0$, lift successively across $D/K^{s+1}\to D/K^s$ for $1\leq s<N$; its kernel $K^s/K^{s+1}$ is square-zero since $2s\geq s+1$. This is a finite induction starting from the given map to $D/K$.

source.place: Tag 00T4, lemma-base-change-smooth; Tag 05D5, lemma-section-smooth, basis lifts and the map modulo the square; Tag 031J, proposition-characterize-formally-smooth

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-formally-smooth-augmentation-truncations] with these exact $R,C,I,f,H$ to get $R[T_1,\ldots,T_r]/H^k\simeq C/I^k$. The first-order bijection and nilpotent lifting hypotheses were established in Step 6. The polynomial quotient is free as an $R$-module on the monomials $T^\alpha$ with $|\alpha|<k$: they span by deleting terms of higher degree, and they are independent because every term in a product of $k$ variables times a polynomial has degree at least $k$, so every element of $H^k$ has all lower coefficients zero. The indexing set is finite, as each exponent is less than $k$ and there are only $r$ variables. By Step 5, $C/I^k=Q\otimes_A R=Q_{\mathfrak p}$, so every prime localization of $Q$ is finite free. For $r=0$ the sole monomial is $1$; for $k=1$ the same is true for any $r$.

source.place: Tag 05D5, lemma-section-smooth, induction on finite quotients; elementary monomial coefficient argument

proof.text: Step 3 gives finite presentation of $Q$ as an $A$-module, and Step 7 gives freeness over every $A_{\mathfrak p}$. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-trf-finite-projective-local-free], so $Q$ is finite projective. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], it is flat over $A$. If $A$ is the zero ring then $B$ and $Q$ are also zero rings, and the same conclusions hold directly; there is no need to choose a prime in an empty spectrum.

source.place: Tag 00NX, lemma-finite-projective, (4) implies (2); Tag 051G, lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat, projective modules are flat in its proof

proof.text: Let $q:\operatorname{Spec}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. On each distinguished open $D(a)$ its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$, with functions $Q_a$. Thus $q_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}Q}$ is the associated module sheaf $\widetilde Q$; the finite generating list of Step 2 gives an epimorphism from a finite free sheaf. Consequently $q$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Its global finite algebra presentation in Step 3 witnesses local finite presentation at every point by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The flat ring map $A\to Q$ gives flat local ring maps $A_{\mathfrak p}\to Q_{\mathfrak q}$, with $\mathfrak p$ the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ in $A$, at every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]; these are the maps $\mathcal O_{S,q(\mathfrak q)}\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}Q,\mathfrak q}$ of local rings, so $q$ is flat at every point and hence flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Definition [def-pc-finite-locally-free] now gives the first conclusion.

source.place: Tag 01WH, definition-integral; Tag 01TP, definition-finite-presentation; Tag 02KB, lemma-finite-flat; algebra.tex Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization

proof.text: Finally [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $Y_n\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(Q\otimes_A A')$ and the ambient base change of $Y$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B'$. The base-changed section corresponds to the explicit retraction $\epsilon'$ in Step 4. Step 5 identifies the former spectrum with $\operatorname{Spec}(B'/(\ker\epsilon')^k)$. Its compatibility with the quotient maps from $B'$ identifies their closed immersions in the ambient base change as well. Since $k=n+1$, this is exactly the asserted infinitesimal neighborhood, including $n=0$.
